truth: Division of land into Mahals belongs to the Mahalwari system, not the Ryotwari system.
I-Tsing visited India in the late 7th century CE, long after Ashoka.
The Virupaksha temple is at Hampi (and Pattadakal) in Karnataka.
The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms became the Government of India Act, 1919.
Aditi, not Prithvi (the earth goddess), was regarded as the mother of the gods.

spot: mentioned the war of succession with his brothers
truth: No Ashokan edict mentions a war of succession with his brothers.
Nalanda was supported by the revenue of about 100 (later about 200) villages.
Nalanda had about 1,500 teachers (about 10,000 students).
The medium of instruction at Nalanda was Sanskrit.
Nikitin visited the Bahmani kingdom in 1469-72, long before Achyuta Deva Raya.
Under Jahangir Kandahar was lost to Persia (1622), not annexed.
CAT members include judicial as well as administrative members.

spot: He has no veto except in case of a tie
truth: True: the Speaker does not vote in the first instance and has only a casting vote in a tie; only option D (presiding during his own removal) is wrong.

spot: majority of all the then members of the Assembly after fourteen days notice
truth: True: Article 179(c) provides removal by a majority of all the then members after 14 days' notice; only option D is wrong.

spot: ceases to be a member of the Assembly
truth: True: under Article 179(a) the Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be a member; only option D is wrong.
The Election Commission can seek transfer or suspension of officials on election duty, but cannot order their dismissal.
Supreme Court judges are removed by the President after an address by both Houses of Parliament (impeachment).

spot: A dispute between two or more States
truth: True: inter-State disputes are within the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction (Article 131); the key pair is II and III.

spot: A dispute between the Government of India and one or more States
truth: True: Centre-State disputes are within the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction (Article 131); the key pair is II and III.

spot: To protect the weaker sections from social injustice
truth: Protecting weaker sections from social injustice is a Directive Principle (Article 46), not a Fundamental Duty.
The Preamble was adopted last, after the rest of the Constitution had been enacted.
The Preamble is not enforceable in courts of law.
The NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure; it follows natural justice.
The NGT sits at five places (Delhi, Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai).
Six communities are notified as minorities (Jains added in 2014), now by the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
The CCI has a chairperson and not more than six members.
Burnt bricks have been found in the late Harappan phase at Bhagwanpura.
Jainas did use Apabhramsa for many important works.
The Sakas were defeated by Chandragupta-II.
The imperial Chola line was founded by Vijayalaya in the 9th century.
Sher Shah collected one-third of the produce as tax.
Sambad Kaumudi was published by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, not Vidyasagar.

spot: Establishment of universities for the first time
truth: The first universities were set up in 1857 under Canning, not Bentinck.

spot: has however been incorporated in the Rules of the House
truth: The whip is in neither the Constitution nor the Rules of the House; it rests on convention (the 1998 Act gives only facilities).

spot: Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs
truth: The government's Chief Whip in the Lok Sabha is the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs.

spot: is not responsible to the leader of the House
truth: The government Chief Whip works under the direction of the Leader of the House.

spot: will have to be referred to the law department for consultation
truth: Law-department consultation and drafting apply to government bills, not private members' bills.

spot: or a member of the government party
truth: A public (government) bill is introduced only by a minister.

spot: upon its approval by the House, a Private Bill would have reflected the policy of the government
truth: A private member's bill reflects the mover's stand, not government policy, even after it is passed.

spot: give effect to certain Directive Principles of State Policy
truth: Reserving such a bill is optional (to gain Article 31C protection); only an Article 288 bill must be reserved.
Such a bill is not mandatorily reserved (Article 255 lets later assent cure it); only an Article 288 bill must be reserved.
Reservation under Article 254(2) is optional; only an Article 288 bill must be reserved.

spot: this does not mean that the CAG can be impeached
truth: The CAG is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge.
The CAG also conducts performance audits.

spot: was established as a Statutory body
truth: The GST Council was created directly as a constitutional body by the 101st Amendment (Article 279A).
Article 279A(10) says defects in appointment do not invalidate the Council's proceedings.

spot: Public Accounts Committee of the Parliament
truth: GST disputes go to a dispute settlement mechanism set up by the GST Council, not the PAC.
The Constitution does not bar retiring Election Commissioners from further government appointment.

spot: treat the Regional Commissioners on par with the Election Commissioners
truth: Anoop Baranwal (2023) dealt with the process of appointing the CEC and ECs, not Regional Commissioners.
The Election Commission was a single-member body until 1989 and multi-member permanently only from 1993.
A law made during President's rule continues until altered or repealed by the State Legislature (Article 357(2)).
The national-interest resolution under Article 249 is passed by the Rajya Sabha.

spot: would be shared between the Centre and the States
truth: Surcharges under Article 271 go wholly to the Centre and are not shared.

spot: were both repealed by same Constitutional Amendment Act
truth: Article 272 was repealed by the 80th Amendment and Article 268A by the 101st Amendment.
Sales tax on petroleum crude is levied and collected by the States (outside GST).
Likely true: PHRA Section 21(6), as amended in 2019, lets the Centre confer UT human-rights functions (other than Delhi) on a State Commission.
Since the 2019 amendment, three NHRC members (one a woman) come from the human-rights-experience category.

spot: seek the opinion of the Supreme Court
truth: The President removes the SHRC Chairperson after a Supreme Court inquiry reports; the statement is substantially correct.
The Commissions cannot inquire into a matter more than one year after the alleged violation.
The Delimitation Commission also identifies seats reserved for SCs and STs.
PM-AJAY is for Scheduled Caste communities.
PM-SYM contributions are shared 50:50 by the worker and the Central Government only.

spot: Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC)
truth: FutureSkills Prime is run by MeitY together with NASSCOM.
Mission Karmayogi has six pillars.
A vote on account is still used, for example in election years.
Amendments to reduce or abolish a tax can be moved on the Finance Bill.

spot: in the case of Money Bills but not in the case of Finance Bills
truth: The President has no suspensive veto over Money Bills; it applies to ordinary (and non-money financial) bills.
Absolute veto is used only in special cases, such as private members' bills or a bill whose government has resigned.

spot: to ensure a system of checks and balances
truth: The veto exists to prevent hasty, ill-considered or unconstitutional legislation.

spot: it has ceased to be operative
truth: Article 31B is still operative; I.R. Coelho only allows basic-structure review of laws added after 24 April 1973.

spot: by the power of the Central Government
truth: Ninth Schedule entries are added by Parliament through constitutional amendment.

spot: includes just States and Union Territories
truth: The 'Union of India' includes only the States; Union Territories fall under the 'Territory of India'.
Both 'Union of India' and 'Territory of India' appear in the Constitution (Article 1).

spot: just the 'Union of India' but not the 'Territory of India'
truth: The First Schedule lists both the States and the Union Territories, so covers the Territory of India too.

spot: by the courts of law rather than by the Constitution
truth: In India equality is guaranteed by the Constitution itself; Dicey's court-based idea describes Britain.
Article 14 contains both 'equality before law' and 'equal protection of laws'.

spot: with the exception of Article 51A(i), which is also applicable to foreigners
truth: All Fundamental Duties apply only to citizens.

spot: irrespective of the existence of legal provisions
truth: The Verma Committee identified existing legal provisions for enforcing the Fundamental Duties.
Fundamental Duties were added only in 1976, after Kesavananda Bharati.

spot: harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
truth: True: Minerva Mills did stress harmony and balance; the explanation itself says III is correct, so the key 'Only III' looks wrong.

spot: only after the prior permission of the President
truth: A private member can introduce a constitutional amendment bill without prior presidential permission.
Article 368 itself provides two types: special majority, and special majority plus ratification by half the States.

spot: The State Legislatures can pass a resolution requesting the Parliament to amend Article 368
truth: States cannot initiate constitutional amendments.
The basic structure doctrine is judge-made (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973).
Kumar Padma Prasad (1992) concerned the independence of the judiciary, not the welfare state.

spot: and not by the Members individually
truth: Parliamentary privileges are enjoyed both collectively by the Houses and individually by members.
Outsiders can also be punished for contempt of the House.
Contempt of the House is the wider concept than breach of privilege.

spot: Introduction and passage of Money Bills
truth: Money Bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha is unequal here.

spot: Initiating the removal of the Vice-President
truth: Only the Rajya Sabha can initiate removal of the Vice-President, a special power rather than equal status.
Sharing of State taxes with Panchayats is decided on the State Finance Commission's advice.
Article 243-I only sets up the State Finance Commission to review and recommend devolution; it gives no such power.
All Panchayats, not only those in Scheduled Areas, can raise their own revenue.
A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

spot: However, the Lok Sabha should not have been dissolved by the time the Bill is returned
truth: A bill returned by the President does not lapse even if the Lok Sabha has been dissolved.
A bill pending in the Rajya Sabha and not passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse.
The Law Commission is a non-statutory advisory body set up by executive order.
The Law Commission gives its views to the Government through the Ministry of Law and Justice.
Law Commission reports are laid before Parliament.
The Law Commission can take up studies suo motu.

spot: a mix of British Fabian Socialism and American Populism
truth: 'Democratic' in the Preamble covers political, social and economic democracy.
'Republic' means India has an elected head of state, the President.
Liberty in the Preamble is qualified, not absolute.
Fraternity originally meant both the dignity of the individual and the unity of the nation.

spot: reserved bonds taken from the G-Sec market
truth: The UIDF is funded from priority sector lending shortfalls.
The UIDF is used by public agencies for urban infrastructure in Tier 2 and 3 cities.

spot: a cluster of Municipal Cooperative Banks
truth: The UIDF is managed by the National Housing Bank.

spot: without the need to be integrated with Primary Health Centres
truth: The Family Doctor Programme works through the PHCs.

truth: True: Sanjeevaiah was Congress President in 1962-64, so this key is doubtful.
The main goal of NREGA is guaranteed wage employment (livelihood security); asset creation is a secondary aim.

Acquired territory can become a new State or a Union Territory, not only part of existing States.
Pre-acquisition laws and rights survive only as far as the Indian state chooses to recognise them.
The Dulhan scheme is limited to poor Muslim brides, not the Muslim community in general.
The key does not accept this cutoff date; only the Rs 50,000 grant to poor Muslim brides is correct.
Only the statement on Rs 50,000 to poor Muslim brides is correct.
Cist burials in Andhra are concentrated in the southern and Rayalaseema/Krishna regions, not Visakhapatnam.
The Vijayapuri Ikshvaku inscriptions do not claim descent from the Ikshvakus of Ayodhya.
The Billa Surgam caves are in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district.
The Kakatiyas rose about 800 years after the Satavahanas, so no marriage alliance was possible.
Rajaraja Narendra's Nandampudi grant was made to Narayana Bhatta.
Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I, married Vimaladitya.
The Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole is attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III's period.
Possibly true: many textbooks credit Prataparudra with the Nayankara system, and the explanation says he expanded it.
The Crescent (1844) was founded by Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty.
Jashuva won the 1964 Sahitya Akademi award for 'Kreestu Charitra'.
The Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was set up in Hyderabad in 1901.
The Communists were the main champions of Visalandhra and linguistic States.
The 97th Amendment added Part IXB on co-operative societies.
The 1998 experimental use of EVMs covered Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.

spot: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India
truth: The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President.

spot: Chief Justice of the concerned State High Court
truth: The committee is the Chief Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM.
The national-interest resolution under Article 249 is passed by the Rajya Sabha.
Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended during an emergency.
PIL grew out of judicial activism.
The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats.
Reservation for backward classes is a voluntary provision left to the States.
Only elected members of Parliament vote in the presidential election.
Only elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies vote in the presidential election.
The Finance Commission is set up under Article 280.
The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President.
The Attorney General receives remuneration as the President may determine.
In a presidential system the President is not accountable to the legislature; that is a parliamentary feature.
Article 243E requires elections within six months of dissolution.
The bar on challenging elections except by petition is in Section 80 of the RPA, 1951.
An election petition must be filed within 45 days of the result.

spot: more than 40% of the State's population
truth: The Sixth Schedule applies only to tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Sixth Schedule areas remain within the executive authority of the State.
The Governor organises and reorganises the autonomous districts.
The State High Court retains jurisdiction in Sixth Schedule areas.

spot: To protect the weaker sections from social injustice
truth: Protecting weaker sections from social injustice is a Directive Principle (Article 46), not a Fundamental Duty.
The Governor could nominate only one Anglo-Indian to the Assembly (Article 333).
European art reached the Mughal court through Portuguese Jesuits and the English.
The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793.
The Second Carnatic War ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754); Yandabo (1826) ended the First Anglo-Burmese War.
The Battle of Chausa (1539) was fought between Humayun and Sher Shah.
The Taiyuni movement was started by Maulana Karamat Ali Jaunpuri.

spot: It prohibited child marriage below the age of 14
truth: The Lex Loci Act 1850 protected converts' inheritance rights; the age-14 bar came with the Sarda Act, 1929.

spot: It extended the prohibition of Sati all across British India
truth: The Lex Loci Act 1850 protected converts' inheritance rights; Sati was banned by Bentinck's 1829 regulation.

spot: It granted the legal recognition to widow marriages
truth: The Lex Loci Act 1850 protected converts' inheritance rights; widow remarriage was legalised in 1856.
The 1869 divorce law was the Indian Divorce Act (for Christians).
Women won about 8% of AP Assembly seats in 2019 (14 of 175).
The AASU-led Assam Movement began in 1979.

spot: to the Bangladeshi Migrants in Assam
truth: The movement sought to detect and deport illegal migrants and to safeguard the Assamese people.
The Assam Movement ended with the Assam Accord of 15 August 1985.

The monthly stipend starts at 18 and the Rs 10 lakh lump sum is paid at 23.

spot: creating job opportunities in the transport sector
truth: YSR Navodayam was a one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans.
